title: POC Weekly - VPC & On‑Prem Stability Tuning (LuminaHealth)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-29 10:00 PDT (17:00Z)
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Alex (Infra), Samir (Security), Jules (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private/VPC+onprem pilot at LuminaHealth. Focus on kernel upgrade fallout, network egress/MTU issues, routing fallbacks, and telemetry gaps.

---

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): "Morning everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — kernel upgrade recap, network egress behavior, routing fallback tuning, telemetry and then next steps. Priya, you still good with this order?"

[00:12] Priya (LuminaHealth): "Yep, that's good. We had a pretty noisy window yesterday evening where a few requests spiked and we saw packet drops, so I'd like to start there if possible."

[00:25] Daniel (Redwood): "Sure, will do. Quick note up front — some of the labels in our telemetry were swapped in the last run so the KV cache warmup metrics looked off; we're treating that as noise for now. We'll share corrected traces."

[00:40] Alex (LuminaHealth): "Yeah, the frontend team reported increased tail latency at p99 during the burst. It coincided with a NAT gateway flapping event, possibly related to MTU fragmentation — we saw logs showing ICMP 'fragmentation needed' from our router."

[01:05] Daniel: "Got it. The MTU mismatch is a classic — when traffic crosses the VPC-to-onprem link sometimes path MTU discovery doesn't play nicely. We recommended enforcing 1400 MTU at the .1 border previously — was that applied?"

[01:22] Jules: "We applied 1460 to match some legacy circuits, maybe that's the reason. I can change to 1400 on a canary link but want to test first."

[01:38] Maya: "Action: Jules to run small MTU canary, but also we should confirm that packet reassembly isn't causing the runtime to stall. Daniel, can you explain what we saw in the kernel logs?"

[01:52] Daniel: "In the kernel v2.1 upgrade we saw an unexpected alloc stall when some jumbo-ish requests hit the batcher and the KV cache fill path triggered memory churn. That produced higher p99 for a subset of calls. We suspect an interaction between the new batching heuristic and the GPU allocation path — it's subtle. The good news is it's reproducible in lab when we replay the pattern."

[02:25] Priya: "So this is the upgrade we rolled out last week? Is the plan to rollback or patch? Our SREs were worried about doing a full rollback mid-business-hours."

[02:40] Daniel: "Short term: rollback is safe and straightforward — we can pin to v2.0 in the canary group if you want an immediate mitigation. Long term: there's a patch that adjusts the batching thresholds and the kernel memory allocator which we believe fixes it without perf loss."

[03:05] Samir (Security): "From a compliance perspective we need a window and clear rollback steps. Also we need to know what logs are retained and whether PII could leak into telemetry during a replay — last week the retention settings were ambiguous."

[03:25] Maya: "Understood. We'll include a rollback runbook with exact CLI steps and expected downtime per shard. On telemetry, we'll scrub PII fields by default for the pilot — Daniel will send the list of fields we scrub."

[03:45] Daniel: "I'll also add a short section on how to rotate KMS keys if you want to replay encrypted logs in dev — but for the pilot we'll keep 30-day retention unless you need longer."

[04:05] Alex: "Also worth flagging: routing fallback — when an onprem node becomes saturated Redwood routed to a hosted fallback which was cheaper but increased cross-region latencies. We need a policy that prefers local latency even if cost is higher for critical routes."

[04:25] Maya: "That's a good point. Our default policy optimizes for cost for non-SLA routes, but you can pin those routes to latency-first. We'll propose a policy config you can audit. Daniel, can you pull suggested thresholds (e.g., switch to fallback only if p95 > 300ms or error rate > 1%)?"

[04:45] Daniel: "Yep, I'll share a YAML snippet. Also recommend tighter circuit-breaker settings because the current ones are wide and sometimes let over-saturated nodes keep taking traffic."

[05:05] Jules: "Question — if we tighten breakers, will that increase the number of fallbacks and thus cost spikes?"

[05:15] Daniel: "Potentially, yes. It's a classic latency vs cost tradeoff. We can set a small cool-down window and a gradated multiplier so brief blips prefer fallback, but sustained load trigger autoscale instead of fallback."

[05:40] Priya: "Ok, that sounds reasonable. We want to avoid cost surprises but not at the expense of user-facing latency. Our success criteria for pilot: p95 under 150ms for normal traffic and p99 under 350ms during bursts. Also cost per 1k tokens should be within the pilot budget we sent last month."

[06:05] Maya: "Noted. We'll codify those SLIs in the pilot playbook. Anything else on routing?"

[06:18] Alex: "No, but telemetry — we discovered missing traces around prefix-cache hits. The dashboard showed zero hits which is impossible."

[06:30] Daniel: "Yep that was the label swap I mentioned — the agent was writing \"prefix_hit_count\" to the wrong metric name due to a small marshaling change. Fix is ready and we'll re-run the telemetry ingest. Expect corrected dashboards by EOD tomorrow."

[06:50] Samir: "Good. On the security checklist, can you confirm SAML SSO works with our identity provider? Last time the attribute mapping was off and group claims weren't honored."

[07:05] Maya: "We've seen that happen on a few customers. We'll send an updated SAML doc and a tested attribute map for Okta/Azure. Also will include RBAC roles mapping for pilot users."

[07:20] Priya: "Perfect. For the SOC2 question — we need the auditor contact and an export of access logs for the last 30 days. Can you supply that?"

[07:30] Maya: "Yes — action item for Samir to confirm auditor contact and we'll prepare the export. Note that exports will contain operational metadata and we'll make sure PII is stripped."

[07:45] Alex: "On the kernel canary timing — we prefer a low-traffic window, 02:00-05:00 UTC looks ok. We just need a rollback plan in <1hr if we see p99 spikes."

[07:58] Daniel: "We can do a staged canary: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with health checks at each step. If p99 jumps > 30% over baseline at any step we automatically rollback. We'll provide the script to enact that."

[08:20] Jules: "I'll run the MTU canary on a small subset tomorrow and attach results. Also I'll share the exact NAT gateway logs from the last event so you can correlate."

[08:40] Maya: "Great. Quick note on pricing — we'll send an updated pilot pricing worksheet that includes a reserved capacity line and an overage estimate if fallbacks are used more than expected."

[08:55] Priya: "That's helpful. We'll review and get back with any budget constraints."

[09:10] Samir: "Question — how are you handling KMS across hosted fallback? Do keys leave our control at any point?"

[09:20] Daniel: "No, for the private pilot the control plane can be configured to use your KMS (customer-managed) for any stored artifacts. For ephemeral runtime encryption we use ephemeral keys that rotate, and we provide logs for key events. We'll send the KMS integration guide."

[09:40] Maya: "Okay let's recap and assign owners. Action items as in the doc. Next steps: schedule lab benchmark for 2026-08-05, canary window target 2026-08-06, and updated pricing + checklist to be sent by 2026-08-02."

[09:58] Priya: "Sounds good. One more tiny thing — can you include a short note in the runbook about how to interpret the KB cache metrics? Our PM got confused by 'hit ratio' vs 'warmup ratio'."

[10:10] Daniel: "We'll add a glossary for metrics and an example traffic pattern mapping."

[10:20] Maya: "Awesome. If no more items, we'll wrap here. Thanks everyone."

[10:25] Alex: "Thanks all."

[10:30] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript contains a few ASR artifacts (e.g., 'sock two' for SOC2, 'quanization' for quantization) and some speaker attribution uncertainty in short crosstalk moments.
